title: Boston Police Department's Motor Vehicle Collisions Data: Summons Issued and ZIP data

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

This request concerns the field interrogation and observation (FIO) datasets that the Boston Police Department has published for 2018 through 2025.

The published datasets for 2020 through 2025 do not include a "Summons Issued" field, and the published 2018 and 2019 datasets appear to have incomplete entries for it. That field is pivotal to my reporting. I am asking the Department to pull the following directly from the database or system in which FIO records are maintained. No files are attached.

I am not seeking home addresses, personal contact information, medical information, officer disciplinary records, or the names or other identifying information of any motorist. I am requesting the following three data sources.

Item 1: For every FIO record with a contact date from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2025, an export containing at least the following three fields: the Field Contact # (or other unique record identifier used in the published datasets), the Contact Date, and the "Summons Issued" value. Please provide a value for every record where one exists in the system, including 2018 and 2019 records that are blank in the published files.

Item 2: For every FIO record from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2025 in which the zip code is blank in the published datasets ("Zip Code" in the 2018-2024 files and "zip" in the 2025 file), an export containing the Field Contact # (or other unique record identifier) and the zip code, to the extent a zip code is recorded in the system.

Item 3: Any data dictionary, field definitions, or other existing documentation describing the "Summons Issued" field, including any record showing when and why the field was removed from the published datasets after 2019.

If any item cannot be produced as written, please tell me what can be, so I can narrow the request.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

title: Request under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act, 5 ILCS 140: FY 2025-26 Audit Records

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Request under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act, 5 ILCS 140: FY 2025-26 Audit Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Under the Illinois Freedom of Information Act, I request copies of the following public records, in electronic format (searchable PDF for documents, native format for spreadsheets), emailed to [your email]. This request is not for a commercial purpose.

Background. The October 26, 2026 Village Board packet (Board Report, packet p. 92) states that “the auditor’s communication is also attached” to the FY 2025-26 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report. It was not included in the packet. At the meeting, Sikich’s representative described a board communication/management letter, an IMRF allocation report, and a total of four reports issued for the year ended April 30, 2026. She also described one material weakness, the status of prior-year comments, and proposed and past audit adjustments.

Records requested (unless stated otherwise, FY ended April 30, 2026):

1.  The auditor’s communication referenced in the Board Report, including the required communications to those charged with governance and any management letter or internal control recommendations, in final form as delivered to the Village and any version presented or distributed to the Board.
2.  All four reports Sikich issued for the year, including the IMRF allocation report. If the Village contends fewer or more than four exist, please identify them.
3.  The schedule or summary of proposed and passed audit adjustments and any uncorrected misstatements provided by Sikich.
4.  The status of prior-year audit comments, including any tracking document, corrective action plan, or written management responses to the FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26 comments.
5.  The management representation letter(s) signed for the FY 2025-26 audit.
6.  All engagement letters, contracts, and amendments between the Village and Sikich covering the FY 2025-26 audit, and any audit planning or scope/timing communication to the Board or Village management.
7.  Records showing why no report under Government Auditing Standards or report on internal control was issued for FY 2025-26, including any analysis of federal award expenditures against the single-audit threshold and any communication with Sikich on the subject.
8.  The “Other reporting required by Government Auditing Standards” report and the report on internal control issued for FY 2024-25.
9.  Communications (emails, letters, text messages, and attachments) from May 1, 2025 through the date of your search between Sikich personnel and any of the following: Jack Knight, Kathleen Morley, the Village’s accounting manager, or any Lauterbach & Amen personnel working for the Village. Limit these to communications concerning (a) the material weakness or other internal control deficiencies, (b) audit adjustments, (c) the Government Auditing Standards or internal control reports, or (d) the delivery of the auditor’s communication to the Board.
10.  Any communication transmitting the auditor’s communication to the Village Board or placing it in a Board packet, and any communication discussing why it was not included in the October 26, 2026 packet.

Statutory points.

-  Public funds records. Section 2.5 makes records relating to the obligation, receipt, and use of public funds public records.
-  Records held by the auditor. If any responsive records are held by Sikich or Lauterbach & Amen rather than the Village, they are public records of the Village under Section 7(2), because those firms perform functions on its behalf. Please obtain them.
-  Publicly cited records. Section 7(1)(f) does not exempt a record “publicly cited and identified by the head of the public body.” The Village Manager’s Board Report cited the auditor’s communication.
-  Exemptions and redactions. If you deny any part of this request, cite the specific exemption (Section 9(a)), explain how it applies, and produce all non-exempt portions with redactions identified (Section 7(1)). Please also provide a log or description of withheld records sufficient to assess the claim.
-  Burden and rolling production. If the Village considers any part of this request unduly burdensome under Section 3(g), I do not require a conference before you proceed. Instead, please produce the responsive records on a rolling basis, releasing a portion each week, beginning with item 1 and moving forward in numerical order, until the request is complete. I am agreeing to this in advance in lieu of any meet-and-confer under Section 3(g). Please do not deny or close the request on burden grounds without first producing on this schedule.
-  Fees. I request a fee waiver under Section 6(c), since this concerns the Village’s audited finances and is in the public interest. If any fees will exceed $[25], please notify me first. I prefer electronic delivery, which should carry no copying charge.
-  Timing. Please acknowledge receipt, and respond within five business days (Section 3(d)). If you invoke a five-business-day extension under Section 3(e), please state the reasons in writing.
-  Preservation. Please preserve all responsive records, including emails and texts on personal devices and accounts used for Village business, while this request is pending.

Please send partial productions as they become available. Thank you.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Concerned Citizen of La Grange

title: Obama Presidential Library: White House and National Security Council Records Concerning the February 13, 2012 Attempted Bombing of an Israeli Embassy Employee's Vehicle in Tbilisi, Georgia, and Its Effect on U.S.-Georgia Relations

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Presidential Records Act, 44 U.S.C. § 2201 et seq., and the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, as applied to Presidential records under 44 U.S.C. § 2204(c) and § 2205, I request access to the records described below, dated February 1, 2012, through July 31, 2012.

Background. On February 13, 2012, an explosive device was found on a vehicle belonging to a locally employed staff member of the Israeli Embassy in Tbilisi, Georgia. This incident was widely covered in the international media. (see: https://www.rferl.org/a/24483526.html). The U.S. Department of State has publicly characterized the Tbilisi incident as "linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Qods Force." [See, "Country Reports on Terrorism 2012": https://2009-2017.state.gov/documents/organization/210204.pdf]. This request concerns the Tbilisi incident specifically. Records addressing Tbilisi together with the New Delhi and Bangkok incidents are responsive. Records addressing only those other incidents are not.

Records requested. Records created, received, or maintained by the National Security Council (including its Georgia/Caucasus, Russia/Eurasia, counterterrorism, Middle East, and Iran-related directorates and the White House Situation Room), the Office of the National Security Advisor, the Office of the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security and Counterterrorism, the Office of the Deputy National Security Advisor, the White House Counsel's Office, and the White House Press Office, concerning:

1. The incident. Situation reports, flash notices, intelligence summaries, briefing memoranda, and email describing the device, the vehicle, the intended target or targets, and the response of Georgian authorities, including the Georgian Ministry of Internal Affairs. This request is specifically requesting a search for photographs, diagrams, imagery, and video of the device, the vehicle, the scene, or the investigation, whether stand-alone or as attachments to, or embedded in, emails, reports, or briefing materials.

2. Attribution. Records discussing or assessing who was responsible, including the basis for linking the incident to the IRGC Qods Force or to Iran, evidence-sharing among U.S., Georgian, and Israeli authorities, and any interagency debate about confidence levels or public attribution.

3. U.S.-Georgia relations. Records assessing the incident's implications for U.S. relations with Georgia and the Saakashvili administration, including: communications with or about Georgian officials concerning the incident; Georgian investigative cooperation; U.S. concerns about Iranian activity in or through Georgia, including Georgia's visa-free regime for Iranian nationals; sanctions-enforcement and counterterrorism cooperation; and talking points or briefing materials for meetings or calls with Georgian officials.

4. Coordination and public response. Records of Principals, Deputies, or Interagency Policy Committee discussions, calls with Israeli counterparts, and talking points or public-affairs guidance concerning the incident.

Custodians. Without limiting the search to these offices or individuals, I ask that it include: the National Security Advisor; the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security and Counterterrorism; the Deputy National Security Advisors; the NSC Senior Directors and Directors for Russia/Eurasia and Georgia, for counterterrorism, and for Israel and Iran; and the NSC Press Office. Specifically requesting that Michael McFaul, Paul Stronksi, Puneet Talwar, John Brennan, Nick Rasmussen and Gary Samore be included in the list of custodians. 

Suggested search terms (in combination): Tbilisi; Georgia; Georgian; Saakashvili; Merabishvili; Ministry of Internal Affairs; Israeli Embassy; Israeli Embassy driver; Hyundai Getz; February 13; Iran; IRGC; Qods Force; Quds Force; Hizballah; Mughniyeh; New Delhi; Bangkok; explosive device; magnetic bomb; visa-free; Iranian nationals.

Format and handling.

• Electronic records. Please search born-digital records, including email and records in the Electronic Records Archive, and not only textual finding aids. Please release in searchable electronic format. Please release any photographs, images, or video in their native digital format, with attachments kept together with their parent emails or reports.

• Classified material. Where responsive records are classified or contain other agencies' equities, please refer them to the originating agencies as needed. Please treat this request as a mandatory declassification review request under Executive Order 13526, § 3.5, as an alternative basis for review of any withheld classified material.

• Withholdings. Please release all reasonably segregable portions. For each withheld record or portion, please provide an itemized description: date, author, recipients, general subject, and the specific restriction or exemption claimed, including any P-restriction under 44 U.S.C. § 2204.

• Scope. Press clippings and published public statements are not requested. This request seeks existing records only and does not ask the Library to create records or perform analysis. If any part is unclear or unduly burdensome, please contact me to narrow it before denying it.

Thank you for the Obama Presidential Library and for the work that the library does each and every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

title: ATO or compliance paperwork for new IRS mobile application

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: ATO or compliance paperwork for new IRS mobile application
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In the recent book "Blockers," the author Michael Lewis relays from Sahil Lavingia (now at the IRS) that he was able to build a new mobile app to replace IRS2Go. In the book, he relays that Sahil spent 2 months working on an application half time and just quietly replaced the official application. "It's just me on my own" is what he quotes Sahil Lavingia as saying.

Needless to say, this would be unusual if true. Every federal application deployed to production (including a mobile application talking to a backend) normally needs to get an Authority to Operate (ATO), which involves collecting evidence that the application conforms to NIST security controls as mandated by law in FISMA. There is an option for agency CIOs to sign a "Risk Acceptance Memo" (RAM) to bypass some of these requirements, but that would require coordination with the CIO.

I would like to request the following materials:
1. Any emails related to the launch of the new IRS application that replaced IRS2Go, either before it was launched or after. These can be limited to those sent to or mailed by Sahil Lavingia and Sam Corcos, or any other position at IRS who would be the Authorizing Official (AO) for this application launch.
2. An Authority to Operate (ATO) or related artifacts like a System Security Plan (SSP) or Security Impact Assessment (SIA) that would have been created as part of the pre-launch authorization to deploy this application to production. It is possible that this could have been created afterwards if the application was launched under a Risk Acceptance Memorandum.
3. Any listing of open areas where this new IRS mobile application is not in compliance with FISMA regulations. These are normally called (Plans of Action & Milestones) or POAMs. They would be around when an ATO was granted.
4. Any sort of Risk Acceptance Memo signed by an Authorizing Official (AO) who signed off on launching the application by assuming responsibility for risks that might impact the applications integrity, confidentiality and availability.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Office of Information Affairs (OIA), is in receipt of your email below. Based on the content of the message, it appears you intended to submit a public records request to a State of Florida agency.

However, your email was directed to a federal agency, namely the USDA. The USDA does not enforce Florida law, nor does it regulate pest control companies licensed under state law.
